correctness.rationale: An explicit vertex model has 20 vertices on the radius sqrt(3) sphere and 3 adjacent edge vectors per vertex with dot product sqrt(5). Its central symmetry yields width twice the support function. The spherical vertex normal cell is bounded by three equally azimuthal great-circle sides with tan inradius q=(3-sqrt(5))/2; side inequalities establish the full angular aperture and sharp polar cutoffs tan(rho)=q, tan(rho*)=2q. With 20 disjoint normal cells, normalized coarea gives density (1) with exact factor 5/sqrt(3). Direct differentiation of arctan(sqrt(1-(1+q^2)s^2)/q)-s beta gives -beta and proves CDF (2), with matching endpoints, total mass one and exactly uniform upper branch. The packaged verify.py reconstructed every vertex, checked angular and CDF properties, compared direct support-function grid evaluations and reproduced the already-published unit-edge second moment; VERIFY_OK on the actual package paths. Finite verification is supplemental to the written universal proof.

value.rationale: The complete unlabeled one-dimensional projection-width law of the regular dodecahedron is a natural intrinsic metric probability invariant; its closed elementary CDF resolves all thresholds rather than a single moment, identifies a nontrivial sharp transition and proves an exactly uniform upper branch containing approximately 65.8276 percent of all directions. Such an explicit law enables quantitative tail and quantile computations and provides a test case for polyhedral stereology and general angular-aperture methods. The result is not merely a cheap normalization or restatement of the known second moment.
